title: Candidate signal thermostat — rapid read
content:
Quick context: 45-minute loop with candidate (Lena Rao) for senior runtime engineer. Goal of loop: signal on model-serving kernels, cache/KV strategies, and tradeoffs for quantized pipelines. This is a fast raw-passback — unpolished, mostly gut and action items.

Immediate gut: green for infrastructure thinking, amber for practical experience shipping quantization/FP16 edgecases at scale. Strong communicator when diagramming; occasionally drifted into academic examples rather than pragmatic tradeoffs.

Notes (timestamped fragments):
- 00:05 — opening: solid problem framing, asked clarifying Qs about our latency SLOs and typical token distributions. Good sign: asks for p95/p99 and request size distribution early.
- 00:12 — KV cache question: proposed a hybrid prefix cache + hot-key LRU approach; suggested TTL-backed invalidation tied to model version tags. Pragmatic, but didn’t mention cross-replica consistency (miss).
- 00:22 — batching strategy: preference for adaptive batching with latency budget (per-tenant): liked the idea of per-route max-latency budget and shaping. Brought up backlog hysteresis to avoid oscillations.
- 00:30 — quantization/accuracy: knows int8 and some per-channel quant approaches, referenced calibration sets. Couldn't immediately recall pitfalls of group-wise quant for attention matrices (flag: had shaky depth here).
- 00:36 — debugging incident: walked through a past outage where a bad kernel selection caused OOMs. Emphasized monitoring, heap snapshots, and safe-rollback playbook. This was concrete and high-signal.

Behavioral + collaboration:
- Comfortable running postmortems; likes blameless docs and toy reproductions for engineers to run locally.
- Prefers pair-programming for tricky kernel optimizations; mentioned mentoring juniors on perf profiling.
- Communication style: concise docs + diagrams, but sometimes over-indexes on nuanced math during cross-functional syncs. Suggest coaching on communicating tradeoffs to PMs/Sales.

Red flags (temperature adjustments):
- Limited recent hands-on with quantized production rollouts (most experience was in prototyping). They have a story but lacks end-to-end metrics instrumentation and rollback automation examples.
- Minor: glossed over multi-tenant noisy-neighbor mitigations when prompted (need concrete isolation designs).

Accelerators / strengths:
- Excellent on routing policies, thoughtful about graceful degradation (model fallbacks, per-tenant routes).
- Strong incident hygiene and debugging instincts — good SRE alignment.
- Good mental model for batching tradeoffs and latency budgets; could own throughput / SLO tuning workstreams.

Hire lean (recommended trajectory):
- Hire for Senior or Staff depending on calibration; if Staff, require a short execution plan for shipping a quantized model gating + rollout runbook in first 3 months.
- If Senior: pair with a quantization SME initially, focus on shipping routing & SLO workstreams.

Suggested follow-ups (actionable):
- Ask for a short take-home or design writeup: "Plan to roll out an int8 quantized variant for a 7B decoder model with zero-downtime rollback and per-tenant fallbacks." Expect ~1–2 pages with metrics to validate. (Assign to Lena within 5 days).
- Pair session: schedule 60m deep dive with quant SME (Maya) to probe group-wise quant pitfalls and kernel fallback logic.
- Request logs/metrics example from candidate: examples of prod dashboards or observability checks used during rollout (prometheus/trace spans).

Calibration notes for panel:
- If other interviewers saw strong hands-on quant rollout stories, tilt hire. If panel flags the same quant gap, consider conditional hire (senior + mentorship plan).
- Compensation/level: candidate expects Staff-level scope; comfortable offering Senior with clear 6-month promotion milestones tied to shipping quant rollout + ownership of per-route SLOs.

Loose agenda for follow-up take-home (for hiring committee):
1) Overview and success metrics (what does success look like — tokens/sec, p99 latency, error budget).
2) Rollout plan (canary %, automatic rollback triggers, telemetry).
3) Safety nets (fallbacks, model-variant routing, degraded-mode behavior).
4) Ops automation (migration scripts, DB/metadata tagging for model versions).
5) Short risk list with mitigation priority.

Raw flags to copy into ATS/scorecard:
- Tech depth: 7/10 (strong infra mental models, weaker group-quant details)
- SRE/ops: 8/10 (excellent incident stories)
- Communication: 7/10 (clear with engineers, needs distillation for PMs)
- Team fit: 8/10 (collaborative, mentoring-minded)

Final quick note: this feels like someone who will ramp fast on routing, latency budgets, and incident hygiene; will need a short mentorship loop for production quantization specifics. My leaning: strong hire with conditional level calibration.

Open questions / things I want to verify in next touch:
- Ask for a concrete rollback automation example (scripts or playbook excerpts).
- Ask how they measured calibration drift after quantization (holdout sets, fidelity metrics).
- Clarify multi-tenant isolation approach for shared GPU pools (did they design tenant throttles or rely on infra layer?).

Slack refs / links I might paste to panel: 
- thread: #runtime-hiring -> "lena-raw-loop-2/13" (create short summary)
- Confluence template: onboarding-rt-new-hires -> include mentorship checkpoints

Notes-to-self: keep this in draft — forward to Arjun + Maya for calibration. If they both agree, push candidate to take-home as described and reconvene.
